# Overview

The rmvpadsl package and its `rmvpa` command describe a whole study in
small YAML files. A
**project file**, `rmvpa.yml`, names the data once. Each file under
`analyses/` describes one analysis with one **verb** (`decode`, `rsa`,
`transfer`, ...), a **scope** (searchlight, regions or whole brain), and
anything that differs from the defaults. Every analysis compiles to an
ordinary rMVPA `model_spec` and runs through `run_searchlight()`,
`run_regional()` or `run_global()`.

Install the command once with `rmvpadsl::install_rmvpa_command("~/.local/bin")`.

```bash
rmvpa new derivatives/lss --target category   # writes rmvpa.yml and analyses/decode_category.yml
rmvpa draft                                   # one subject, quick, no permutations
rmvpa run                                     # checks, then runs every subject x analysis
```

The same steps from R:

```{r}
rmvpa_new("derivatives/lss", target = "category")
rmvpa_run(".", draft = TRUE)
rmvpa_run(".")
```

# The project file

```yaml
rmvpa: "0.1"
data:
  bids: derivatives/lss
  space: MNI152NLin2009cAsym
  mask: brain
  sets:
    objects:
      task: objects
      keep: { response: { in: [hit, correct_rejection] } }
    encoding:  { task: memory, acq: encoding }
    retrieval: { task: memory, acq: retrieval }
folds:
  by: run
  assert: [classes_in_every_fold]
run:
  workers: 8
  seed: 20261104
```

* `data.bids` is a BIDS-derivatives folder holding beta series. For subject
  `XX` and a set, the beta images are the files under `sub-XX/` whose names
  carry the set's entities and `space-<space>` and end in `_betas.nii.gz`.
  Each image has a design table with the same name ending in `_betas.tsv`,
  one row per volume. Several matching files (one per run) are concatenated
  in run order, and a `run` column is added from the `run-` entity.
* Instead of `bids`, `data.files` gives explicit templates, for example
  `betas: betas/sub-{subject}_task-{task}_betas.nii.gz`.
* `data.mask` is a `desc-` label (`brain` finds `*_desc-brain_mask.nii.gz`)
  or a path.
* Each **set** selects beta series by BIDS entities. `keep` filters design
  rows before any folds are built. It accepts only equality or `{in: [...]}`.
* All file paths except `extends` are relative to the project root.

# Analysis files

```yaml
# analyses/decode_category.yml
extends: ../rmvpa.yml
decode:
  set: objects
  target: category
scope:
  searchlight: { radius: 6 }
```

`set:` can be left out when the project defines a single set. Each key has
exactly one form; there are no shorthands, and unknown keys are errors with a
suggestion:

```
analyses/decode_category.yml: decode.targte: unknown key 'targte'; did you mean 'target'?
```

`rmvpa explain decode_category` prints the resolved analysis, with every
default filled in and each value tagged by its origin. The output is itself a
valid analysis file:

```yaml
extends: ../rmvpa.yml
decode:
  method: sda_notune                           # default@0.1
  set: objects                                 # analysis
  target: category                             # analysis
folds:
  by: run                                      # project
  scheme: leave_one_out                        # default@0.1
  assert: [classes_in_every_fold]              # project
scope:
  searchlight:
    sampling: standard                         # default@0.1
    iterations: 4                              # default@0.1
    radius: 6                                  # analysis
inference:
  test: permutation                            # default@0.1
  permutations: 100                            # default@0.1
  ...
```

Inheritance has one rule: maps merge key by key, and a scalar or list in the
analysis replaces the project value. `~` removes an inherited key. `explain`
lists each replaced list and each removal.

# Verbs

A verb fixes which keys an analysis takes. `method:` picks the algorithm from
a closed list. `rmvpa verbs` prints the table.

| Verb | Required keys | `method` | Compiles to | Scopes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `decode` | target | a registered classifier (`rmvpa classifiers`) | `mvpa_model` | all |
| `transfer` | train_set, test_set, target | naive, remap_rrr, subspace_alignment, or a classifier | `naive_xdec_model`, `remap_rrr_model`, `subspace_alignment_model`, `mvpa_model` | searchlight, regions |
| `rsa` | item, predictors | pearson, spearman, lm, rfit | `rsa_design` + `rsa_model` | searchlight, regions |
| `rsa_vector` | item, distances | pearson, spearman | `vector_rsa_model` | searchlight, regions |
| `rsa_contrast` | item, contrasts | average, L2_norm, crossnobis | `msreve_design` + `contrast_rsa_model` | searchlight |
| `rsa_feature` | item, feature_spaces | pls, pca, glmnet, ridge | `feature_rsa_model` | searchlight, regions |
| `rsa_era` | train_set, test_set, link | similarity, partition | `era_rsa_model`, `era_partition_model` | searchlight, regions |
| `rsa_connect` | item, seed_region | | `repnet_model` | searchlight, regions |
| `rsa_mediate` | item, predictor, outcome | | `repmed_model` | searchlight, regions |
| `encode` | item, feature_spaces | banded_ridge | `banded_ridge_model` | whole_brain (voxelwise) |
| `pattern` | target | | `pattern_model` | all |
| `manova` | terms | | `manova_model` | searchlight, regions |
| `custom` | r_file | | your `build_spec(dataset, design, config)` | all |

Shared role names mean the same thing in every verb:

* `target`: the design column to predict.
* `item`: the design column naming the stimulus that indexes RDM and
  feature-table rows.
* `link`: the column that pairs rows across two sets.
* `predictors` and `nuisance`: named RDM tables (CSV or TSV, item names in
  the first column).

RDMs and feature tables are written per item. For `rsa` they are expanded to
trial level, because `rsa_model` compares trial patterns.

# Inference

The language never invents a null. The default for each verb and scope is
the null that rMVPA actually computes:

| Analysis | searchlight | regions | whole_brain |
|---|---|---|---|
| `decode` | pooled permutation null, adjusted by searchlight size, FDR over centres | none | none |
| `rsa` | permutation; joint null with regression and more than one predictor | none | none |
| `rsa_vector`, `rsa_feature` | model-internal permutations, uncorrected | model-internal, uncorrected | none |
| everything else | none | none | none |

"none" means the outputs are stamped *descriptive only*. Writing
`inference: { test: permutation }` for one of those cells is an error that
names the missing R piece. Searchlight permutations default to 100 (rMVPA's
own default is 5). `rmvpa check` warns when model-internal permutations are
below 1000.

# Checking, running and re-running

* `rmvpa check` validates every file. Then for each subject it finds the input
  files, reads the design tables (not the images), checks referenced columns,
  runs the fold assertions, compares the atlas grid with the mask, and
  estimates the number of passes. It fits nothing.
* `rmvpa run` always checks first. It asks before a large run (pass `--yes`
  to skip the prompt) and then runs each subject x analysis cell.
* A cell re-runs only when the hash of its resolved analysis or its input
  files changes. `rmvpa status` shows `done`, `stale` or `missing` for every
  cell.
* `rmvpa draft` runs the first subject with a one-iteration randomized
  searchlight and no permutations, into `derivatives/rmvpa-draft/`.

Fold assertions come from a closed list:

| Assertion | Applies to |
|---|---|
| `classes_in_every_fold` | decode, transfer, pattern |
| `no_item_across_folds` | verbs with `item` |
| `one_run_per_fold` | all |
| `train_test_disjoint_runs` | transfer, rsa_era |

An assertion that does not apply to a verb is an error. Repeated stimuli
across runs are common and legitimate, so `rmvpa new` writes only
`classes_in_every_fold`.

# Outputs and provenance

Results go to `derivatives/rmvpa/<analysis>/sub-<label>/`:

```
sub-01_task-objects_space-MNI_desc-decodecategory_stat-Accuracy_statmap.nii.gz
sub-01_task-objects_space-MNI_desc-decodecategory_stat-Accuracyp_statmap.nii.gz
sub-01_task-objects_space-MNI_desc-decodecategory_regions.tsv      # regions scope
sub-01_task-objects_space-MNI_desc-decodecategory_rmvpa.json      # sidecar
```

The JSON sidecar records:

* the resolved analysis and its hash, and the DSL and rMVPA versions;
* the null actually used, with every permutation setting and the smallest
  attainable p;
* chance levels (AUC is reported chance-centred, so its chance is 0);
* fold assertions, and rows before and after `keep`;
* the MD5 of every input file;
* lock status, and whether the run was a draft.

# Preregistration

`rmvpa lock` appends the hash of each resolved analysis to `rmvpa.lock`. The
file is append-only. Later outputs are stamped `lock: match`, `mismatch` or
`none`. Locking is optional and does not affect caching.

# Escape hatch

For anything the verbs do not cover, `custom:` sources an R file. Its
builder, `build_spec(dataset, design, config)`, receives the loaded
`mvpa_dataset` and the train design table, and must return a `model_spec`:

```yaml
extends: ../rmvpa.yml
custom:
  set: objects
  r_file: specs/build_spec.R
scope:
  regions: { atlas: atlas/space-MNI_atlas-Schaefer200_dseg.nii.gz }
```

`rmvpa_compile(".", "decode_category", "01")` returns the compiled
`model_spec` for one subject, so you can inspect or run it by hand.

# Migrating from rmvpa-searchlight and rmvpa-regional

`rmvpa migrate old_config.yaml --dir new_project` converts a single-set config
for the old commands into a project with explicit file paths and one
analysis. rMVPA's own `rmvpa-searchlight` and `rmvpa-regional` keep working
unchanged.

# Not in DSL 0.1

* Trial-wise ITEM decoding needs TR-level time series, which the beta-series
  data model does not describe.
* Permutation nulls for regions and whole brain need
  `run_permutation_regional()` first.
* Group-level tests on the chance-centred per-subject maps are also left for
  later.
